answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the basalt check immediately, the atlas audit keeps the resolved set and the cipher replay publishes exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 35 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 35 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission.
